canonical_claim: RESURRECT-REUPLOAD-ORPHAN is prevented by tracking the `(hash, token)` incarnation so a replacement token starts a fresh condemnation cycle.
Probe cleanup must be HEAD-gated before issuing `deleteExact`; otherwise AWS returns 400 `InvalidArgument` when cleanup sends an empty `If-Match` after the probe keys were already deleted.

GCS `CompleteMultipartUpload` silently ignores `x-goog-if-generation-match`, so conditional writes must not use multipart there; `Compose` enforces the precondition, making multipart-to-temp-key followed by `Compose(temp -> final)` and temp deletion the production path for large blobs. GCS `CompleteMultipartUpload` silently ignores `x-goog-if-generation-match`, while `Compose` enforces it; conditional writes therefore must not use multipart finalize, with unconditional multipart to a temporary key followed by conditional `Compose` as the production-grade large-blob path. On GCS, `CompleteMultipartUpload` silently ignores `x-goog-if-generation-match` (both a `0`-against-existing and a wrong-generation precondition return 200 and overwrite), so conditional writes must not use multipart on GCS; `Compose` does enforce the precondition, so the production-grade large-blob path on GCS is: unconditional multipart-to-temporary-key, then a preconditioned `Compose(temp -> final)`, then delete the temp key.

On GCS, non-numeric probe wrong tokens caused the dialect format guard to fail closed; LIST-derived MD5 ETags poisoned `If-Match` in GC and are disabled on generation stores; and `Expect: 100-continue` initially missed the dialect header, creating a B118-class stall risk. Three bugs were found and fixed while validating the GCS Generation binding end-to-end: (1) probe wrong-tokens were non-numeric, so the dialect's format guard killed the mount; (2) LIST-derived tokens on GCS are MD5 ETags (XML LIST bodies are not rewritten to generations), which would poison `If-Match` in GC, so list-derived tokens are disabled on generation-token stores; (3) the `Expect: 100-continue` handling did not recognize the GCS dialect header, creating a B118-class stall risk.

The CAS write path spills the entire object to local `cas_scratch` for hash-before-upload, so writing a part requires free local disk at least as large as the part even though the S3 upload streams; the proposed fix is in-stream hashing.

`Build::copyForwardFromCondemned` incorrectly verified payloads with one-shot `CityHash128`, while the pool uses streaming `HashingWriteBuffer` hashing in 2048-byte blocks (`DBMS_DEFAULT_HASHING_BLOCK_SIZE`); payloads larger than 2048 bytes were falsely rejected. Copy-forward verification must recompute the content hash with `HashingReadBuffer` over the payload and the same `getHexUIntLowercase` to `hexToU128` conversion used by the write path.
P4 was an S3 multipart completion failure where 48 ETags were rejected after a writer kill, suggesting stale multipart-session reuse across incarnations.
The S13 merge-finalize retry path re-uploaded blobs on every attempt during persistent 503s, growing the pool by 47 GB in eight minutes after the workload stopped.
When token A was condemned and a writer re-uploaded token B at the same blob key, exact-token deletion of A found B and no-op'd, while the hash-keyed fold failed to condemn B, leaving B orphaned.
`PocoHTTPClient` applies `request_timeout_ms` as socket send/receive timeouts rather than one strict wall-clock deadline for the complete logical S3 operation.
`CasGenerationSeal` decodes `RefNsCleanupState` and `TokenType` with unchecked `static_cast`, allowing invalid wire values to reach GC decision logic.

The generic `clonePart` path uses `copyDirectoryContent` and `IDisk::copyFile` to create a fresh autocommit transaction per file, and a later content file raises `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` with `Autocommit writes are not supported for content part files`.

Review finding №1 is a partial real fix: conditional S3 copy can fall back to unconditional copying, but the common single-operation path is probe-guarded and the remaining gap is multipart copies larger than 32 MiB. The CAS review triage confirmed that conditional S3 copy could silently fall back to an unconditional write; task T8 fixed it in commit `a7d171f1d3e`. `copyObjectConditional` can fall back to an unconditional read/write copy after `AccessDenied` or unsupported multipart-copy paths, allowing a concurrent CAS promotion to be overwritten; conditional operations must fail closed. When `if_none_match` is present, both S3 copy fallback branches must rethrow the original error rather than degrade to an unconditional read/write copy.

Review finding №19 is a low-harm but real wire-contract issue: conditional mutations send only `Token.value`, so callers should reject mismatched token types before any conditional operation. Native conditional mutations ignore `Token.type` and send only `Token.value`, allowing a same-text token from a different token dialect to authorize a mutation. Emulated object tokens must use the underlying object's etag value with `TokenType::Emulated`, and conditional operations must reject an expected token whose type differs from the backend's minting type.

Review finding №23 is real: CA `truncateFile` silently succeeds without changing bytes, so it should raise `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` because immutable blobs require whole-file replacement. CA `truncateFile` must throw `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` because blobs are immutable and whole-file rewrites replace the staged entry.

Review finding №24 is real: `unlinkFile` ignores `if_exists`, so removing a nonexistent file can silently succeed instead of raising `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` for the non-`if_exists` API. CA `unlinkFile` must raise `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` for a missing committed path when `if_exists` is false and be a no-op when `if_exists` is true.

CAS blob freshness-meta writes on the INSERT/merge hot path bypass the budgeted `CasRequestController`: `putMetaIfAbsent`, `casMeta`, and `deleteMetaExact` call backend conditional operations directly. S22 exposed a product bug: conditional freshness-meta sidecar writes for CAS blob keys such as `soak_pool/blobs/ch128/<xx>/<hash>.meta` bypassed the CAS retry controller, so an injected S3 `SlowDown` escaped as HTTP 500 with `S3_ERROR` code 499. `writeFreshMetaClean`, `writeResurrectMetaClean`, `putMetaIfAbsent`, and `casMeta` call `backend.casPut(...)` directly through `CasBlobMeta.cpp`, while `conditionalWriteSettings()` forces `s3_max_unexpected_write_error_retries_override = 1`, leaving freshness-meta writes with zero controller retries. A five-hour CA soak validation round found a genuine PRODUCT BUG in S22: `CasBlobMeta.cpp`'s `putMetaIfAbsent`/`casMeta`/`deleteMetaExact` hit the backend directly, the only hot-path conditional-write class outside `CasRequestController`, so an injected `SlowDown` fault gets one SDK attempt with zero controller-level retries and escapes to the client as an HTTP 500; the fix reroutes these through the controller and adds a new controlled If-Match variant plus a fault gtest.

The observed CAS ref-prefix enumeration omitted two objects that had been durable for nineteen seconds while returning a third object written 2.2 milliseconds after them; the store-side mechanism remains unknown.

Historical and live holes form short adjacent runs rather than dropped pages: one historical firing had 13 holes across two namespaces, and the live capture had two adjacent holes immediately below the witness id `0x1430e`.

Default CAS deduplication relies on collision-prone `CityHash128` without rehashing or comparing stored bytes, so an untrusted shared-pool writer can substitute attacker-controlled bytes after a chosen collision. Pool-global deduplication uses non-cryptographic `CityHash128` content keys without normal read-time payload rehashing, so a collision can poison a blob across tables or tenants that share a pool.
The emulated Local backend returns monotonic emulation tokens for exact operations but ETag/mtime tokens from LIST, so GC exact deletes based on listing tokens fail.
`LocalObjectStorage` writes final blob keys with `O_TRUNC` and no atomic PUT semantics, so ENOSPC or termination can leave a partial body that a later `putIfAbsent` treats as an existing object.

An inline-only CA part could reach `publishStaging` with nonempty staged entries and `st.build == nullptr`, causing a `LOGICAL_ERROR`; the inline write path now calls `buildFor(route, st)` so an all-inline part has a `Build`.

The worklog observed incomplete LIST answers for the same ref-log prefix: `0x1430c` and `0x1430d` were present by `HEAD` but omitted from a fold scan after `0x1430e`, and deletion, append ordering, and not-yet-landed writes were excluded for that occurrence.
HEAD-first deduplication makes an existing content key observably cheaper to write, allowing an inserter to test whether candidate content already exists anywhere in a pool shared across namespaces.

During the S3-native-staging end-to-end validation on RustFS, staged blobs were found to be stored without the 256-byte `CABL` envelope header — a data-corrupting bug invisible to 17 in-memory unit tests — fixed by dropping `logical_size`/`logical_hash` from the staging path and writing the header directly into the staging object ahead of hashing; a related fix introduced fresh-tag resurrect to close an `INV_NO_RETURN` self-condemn hole this staging change exposed.

`WriteSettings.h` grew six CA-driven fields including `shared_ptr<const S3::Client> s3_client_override`, and the struct's defaulted `operator==` now compares that shared_ptr by identity; because `WriteSettings` is copied on hot write paths, this adds atomic refcount traffic and a widened recompile blast radius, with surprising equality semantics on the client pointer.

412/`PreconditionFailed` detection is duplicated across 3-4 sites (`Client::RetryStrategy`, `removeObjectIfTokenMatches`, `copyObjectConditional`) via `exc.getExceptionName()=="PreconditionFailed" || message.find("PreconditionFailed")`, so a store with a differently-worded error body could silently misclassify a precondition failure; the fix is a shared `S3Exception::isPreconditionFailed()` helper.

Risk register #14 (Med-Low, confirmed): `CasXXH3.h:25` includes xxHash via a 6-level relative path (no CMake target) specifically to dodge lz4's bundled copy, which breaks silently on file moves or include-order changes. Suggested action: add a `ch_contrib::xxhash` include dir.
B92 requires an adopted leaf to carry its real `blob_size` rather than a placeholder or zero value.

A blob is identified by the pair BlobRef = (algo, digest), never by a bare digest, because multiple 16-byte hash algorithms can coexist. A blob is identified by the pair `BlobHashAlgo` and `BlobDigest`; a bare digest is not an identity because pools may mix `CityHash128`, `XXH3_128`, and `Sha256`. The immutable blob identity in a mixed-algorithm pool is the pair `BlobRef{algo, digest}`; a bare digest is not a blob identity and equal digest values under different algorithms name different objects.
Blob safety requires a fresh in-body incarnation_tag for every upload, a backend token, and exact-token deletion; resurrecting a condemned blob re-uploads from the writer's source with a fresh tag.
A BlobDigest is a fixed 32-byte tail-zero value whose meaningful length is 16 bytes for ch128 and xxh3 and 32 bytes for sha256.
The backend contract requires deleteExact to remove only the matching incarnation and requires TOKEN⟹CONTENT so a token match implies unchanged bytes for manifest cache reuse.

MetaState::Clean means a blob is referenceable and MetaState::Condemned means GC has marked its in-degree zero; GC writes Condemned before deleting the body, and absent metadata is treated as live. GC's writer freshness marker is a per-hash `.meta` object with `Clean` and `Condemned` states; a writer that reads `Condemned` aborts reuse and re-uploads from source. Per-hash freshness metadata uses magic `CAMT` and two states: `Clean = 0` means referenceable body present, and `Condemned = 1` means GC marked zero in-degree while the body remains present for possible CAS resurrection.
A part write proceeds as writeFile() × N followed by precommitAdd(), putBlob() × N, and promote().
stageManifest writes the manifest with putIfAbsentStream before precommitAdd, and no blob body HEAD is required before the precommit CAS.

The revival invariant forbids reading a condemned or vanished blob to revive it; revival re-uploads the writer's own source bytes with a fresh incarnation. A condemned blob is never adopted or server-side-copied; it is recreated from the writer's own source bytes under a fresh `incarnation_tag`.

`deleteExact(blobKey, token)` treats `Deleted`, `TokenMismatch`, and `NotFound` as successful terminal outcomes for the corresponding delete attempt. `deleteExact(hash, token)` treats `Deleted`, `TokenMismatch`, and `NotFound` as completed delete outcomes; a token mismatch means a writer recreated a fresh live incarnation, which can be re-condemned by a later round.

The blob envelope has a fixed 256-byte header with a 94-byte core containing `magic`, `writer_version`, `compatibility_version`, `hash_algo`, `flags`, `header_len`, `logical_size`, `logical_hash`, `domain_id`, `incarnation_tag`, `build_id`, and `header_hash`.
The envelope core is never extended; new fields go into the `[94, header_len)` TLV area and `header_len` is padded to an 8-byte multiple with a pool payload offset of 256 bytes.
`compatibility_version > G_BUILD` decodes as `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`, bad magic or header hash decodes as `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and unknown critical TLVs decode as `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`.

CAS blob hashing is streaming, and `CityHash128` preserves ClickHouse's legacy chunked `CityHash128WithSeed` convention rather than using a one-shot hash for large inputs. Blob identity is the streaming chunked hash of raw payload bytes using 2048-byte `DBMS_DEFAULT_HASHING_BLOCK_SIZE` blocks, not a one-shot hash of the whole payload.

A blob hash covers `[header_len, EOF)` payload bytes and excludes the envelope header and incarnation zone. A blob's incarnation zone is excluded from logical_hash, so a new physical incarnation can have a different token without changing the blob id
`Cas::Backend` exposes token-aware `get`, `getStream`, `head`, `putIfAbsent`, `putIfAbsentStream`, `putOverwrite`, `casPut`, `deleteExact`, and `list`, plus `supportsListTokens`.

`deleteExact(key, token)` removes only the matching incarnation and returns `TokenMismatch` without changing the object when the token differs. `deleteExact(key, token)` deletes only the named object incarnation; `TokenMismatch` leaves the object readable.
S3 and Azure use content-derived ETags as incarnation tokens, allowing CA to use the PUT response ETag without a follow-up HEAD; dedup reuse after `PreconditionFailed` still needs a HEAD.
GCS generation tokens are not content-derived, so generation stores disable LIST-token shortcuts and require the probed conditional dialect and token semantics.
Generation-1 format evolution uses `compatibility_version` write-down-to-floor: additive protobuf fields are skipped by old readers, while breaking binary changes require a floor-gated branch.
`getResultObjectETag()` exposes the PUT or multipart-completion ETag after the upload finalize barrier so CA can record an incarnation token without a follow-up HEAD.

Native conditional copy uses `If-None-Match: *`; a 412 means the destination already exists and returns `{created=false}`, while disabling native copy fails with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` instead of doing an unconditional copy.
Token-exact object deletion maps `If-Match` 412 to `TokenMismatch`, 404 to `NotFound`, and other errors to exceptions.

GCS conditional semantics require the native `GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256` dialect because GCS S3-compatible SigV4 silently ignores `If-None-Match` and `If-Match`. Conditional S3 PUT/COPY operations use `If-Match` and `If-None-Match`, while GCS uses `x-goog-if-generation-match` with native GOOG4 signing because AWS SigV4 `If-Match` semantics are insufficient for GCS.

GCS maps `If-None-Match: *` to `x-goog-if-generation-match: 0`, maps numeric `If-Match` to the corresponding generation condition, and rejects conditional multipart completion. The GCS conditional dialect maps `If-None-Match: *` to `x-goog-if-generation-match: 0` and `If-Match: "<digits>"` to `x-goog-if-generation-match: <digits>` at the HTTP boundary.
Unknown or future format versions are expected to raise `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`; the test helper comment claiming `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` is stale.

Any action that stops a token from being current must add the displaced token to `deadTok[h]`, and revalidation mode must check the current physical token in the same CAS. Any action that stops a token being current, including delete-land, `WResurrect`, and `WOverwrite`, must push the displaced token into `deadTok[h]`; publish must revalidate the dependency's current physical state rather than only the originally observed token.
The fix for resurrect-reupload orphan re-condemns the current token when a prior retired entry's token differs, and emits `blob_retire_replaced`.
On the baseline novel write path, each novel blob uses one conditional `PUT` with `If-None-Match:*`.
On the optimized warm-cache write path, each cached dedup hit performs a `HEAD` and a per-hash `.meta` point-read `GET` instead of a body upload.
A stale dedup-cache hit falls through from `HEAD` 404 to a normal conditional `PUT`.

The shared CAS data plane is shared-nothing: servers share only the content-addressed `blobs/` space, and correctness requires conditional writes on individual objects rather than a serializable metadata service.

A stored blob object consists of a 256-byte envelope header followed by its payload; the header carries a fresh random `incarnation_tag` for each upload attempt, while the digest covers only the payload. A CABL blob has a fixed-size CasEnvelope header followed by raw payload bytes, with blob_header_len normally 256 and an envelope core of 94 bytes
Every destructive CAS operation names the exact incarnation token it intends to remove.
`putIfAbsent` precondition failure is an outcome rather than an exception, while a wrong-dialect token is rejected locally before a conditional overwrite reaches the wire.

A blob upload retries at most 8 times, mints a fresh `incarnation_tag` per attempt, verifies the source byte count, and throws retry-later without acknowledging anything when the outcome remains unresolved.

When two writers upload identical content, one `If-None-Match: *` request succeeds and the other receives 412, HEADs the object, reads `.meta`, and adopts the winner's token after its own precommit edge is durable.
All `adoptEvidence` dependencies originate from a committed manifest and therefore represent reference transfer from a currently reachable object, not resurrection of garbage.
A copy-forward overwrite uses `putOverwrite(key, bytes, expected = observed token)`; `PreconditionFailed` triggers a HEAD and bounded re-evaluation, while eight failed attempts end in `ABORTED`.

At the commit gate, a blob incarnation whose `(hash, current_token)` appears in the retired list must be recreated from build-local source with a token-conditional overwrite; the retired token is never referenced.
`Backend::get(key, Range)` must perform a true ranged object-storage read using `seek` and a bounded read window, not read the whole object and apply `substr` afterward.

`Backend::getStream(const String & key, Range range = {})` returns `{std::unique_ptr<ReadBuffer>, Token}` as a forward-only read of a write-once object; mutable objects such as shards, `gc/state`, and mounts must continue using `get`.
GCS returns the object incarnation token in every PUT and HEAD response as `x-goog-generation`, eliminating the need for a post-PUT HEAD.

GCS generation mismatches return HTTP 412 with the literal XML body code `PreconditionFailed`, so the existing ClickHouse detectors `finalizeConditionalWrite` and `removeObjectIfTokenMatches` require no change.
The GCS conditional dialect rewrites a response's `x-goog-generation` to a quoted `ETag`, allowing existing ETag token plumbing, `HeadResult.token`, and token-exact deletion to remain unchanged.
`signGOOG4` signs the final request with `host` and every `x-goog-*` header, sets `x-goog-content-sha256: UNSIGNED-PAYLOAD` and `x-goog-date`, and uses the scope terminator `goog4_request`.
The GOOG4 key derivation is `HMAC("GOOG4"+secret, date) → "auto" → "storage" → "goog4_request"`, and the signer includes canonical query parameters such as multipart and list parameters.

`applyGcsConditionalDialectToRequest` drops AWS authentication artifacts including `Authorization`, `X-Amz-Date`, `x-amz-content-sha256`, and `x-amz-security-token`, then renames remaining `x-amz-*` headers to `x-goog-*`.
`S3ObjectStorage` reports `TokenType::Generation` when its client uses the GCS conditional dialect; otherwise CAS tokens remain `TokenType::ETag`.

The CAS capability probe calls `Backend::checkStorePreconditions` before its operation battery; the default hook is a no-op. `runCapabilityProbe` performs an eight-step backend capability battery on throwaway keys and fails closed with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.
`PocoHTTPClientGCSHMAC` applies the GCS conditional dialect before GOOG4 signing, while `PocoHTTPClientGCPOAuth` applies the dialect before injecting the Bearer authorization header.
`conditionalOpsUseGenerationTokens()` is a virtual object-storage capability that defaults to `false`; `S3ObjectStorage` returns whether its client uses the GCS conditional dialect.
The GCS conditional-write path must never allow `CompleteMultipartUpload`; `WriteBufferFromS3` throws `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` before starting multipart when `s3_force_single_part_upload` is set.
The generation-binding implementation leaves the 412 `PreconditionFailed` detection code untouched because GCS and AWS expose the same body code.
GCS XML API with GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256 signing enforces the required conditional operations, using `x-goog-if-generation-match` and returning `x-goog-generation` as the token.
Writers consult `store->retireView().isCondemnedToken(hash, token)`; recording the current resurrected token B as condemned makes a later dedup hit re-upload instead of adopting B.
For blob storage objects, the stored object length is the payload length, while `getBlobViewPlan` applies the blob header offset and file window for byte reads.
Blob payload bytes are not cached; a committed view naming a missing blob still surfaces an exception when the payload is read.
The validated CAS safety core is one key per hash plus an in-body incarnation_tag and exact-token body deletion; the freshness-meta work left that core unchanged.
BlobSource retains a size and a closure that rereads a pending-blob temporary file; it does not retain the payload in memory, and the temporary file remains until commit cleanup after promote.
The tokened promote revalidation uses a bounded loop of up to eight attempts, re-HEADing after each source upload and failing with ABORTED if the leaf remains absent or condemned.
uploadFromSource re-uploads the writer's bytes through head, putIfAbsentStream, and putOverwrite without backend().get, preserving INV-1.
A source-backed condemned or absent blob is re-uploaded and rechecked in a bounded loop; a tokened dependency without a retained source remains an ABORTED fail-closed backstop.
The tokenless copy-forward GET remains the sole documented exception to the never-read-the-dying-object rule; tokened resurrection uses uploadFromSource instead.
The in-closure condemned branch chooses uploadFromSource for a tokened source, copyForwardFromCondemned for a copy-forwardable tokenless dependency, and ABORTED otherwise.
copyForwardFromCondemned verifies the condemned payload hash against the content key and republishes a fresh incarnation using token-conditional putOverwrite.
GC deletes blob bodies with DELETE If-Match against the condemn-time body token; resurrecting with a fresh in-body tag changes the etag so the old exact-token delete misses.
The per-hash .meta object is a two-state clean/condemned freshness marker with condemn_round and size; it is not the delete linearizer and is not read by the data path.

Fresh upload writes the body before a clean meta; dedup adoption point-reads the meta and adopts clean or absent metadata, while condemned metadata triggers resurrection. The writer point-reads metadata for condemned status, writes clean metadata after fresh body upload or resurrection, and may best-effort create clean metadata when adopting a present body with absent metadata.

Tokenless copy-forward reads a still-present condemned body only for an adoptEvidence dependency with an independent committed source owner, verifies the payload hash, and republishes a fresh incarnation.
A condemned non-tokened leaf is copy-forwarded only when isCopyForwardableTokenless is true; otherwise promote throws ABORTED.
The final BlobMeta shape is version, state in {clean, condemned}, condemn_round, and size; Tombstone and the incarnation nonce are excluded because metadata is not the delete linearizer.

Meta codec decoding fails closed on bad magic, version, length, or an invalid state value. The meta codec uses magic `CAMT`, version 2, state, `condemn_round`, size, and a 16-byte `incarnation` field; decoding rejects bad magic, unsupported version, invalid state, wrong length, and the old pre-incarnation length with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

The shared meta-ops API consists of `loadMeta`, `putMetaIfAbsent`, `casMeta`, and `deleteMetaExact`; `loadMeta` returns an optional `LoadedMeta` containing the decoded `BlobMeta` and etag, and an absent meta returns `nullopt`.
`WriterId` renders as two fixed-width 16-digit lower-case hexadecimal components, for example `0000000000000007-000000000000008e`; upper-case, shortened, zero, and overflowing forms are rejected.
Body-bearing ref-log records use `_log/<incarnation>/<seq>/tx/<body_hash>.proto`, where `body_hash` is the lower-case 32-digit hexadecimal `CityHash128` of the deterministic stored bytes.
The source-edge run format defines `kEdgeActive = 0x01`, `kZeroMarker = 0x00`, `kCondemned = 0x02`, and `kSourceEdgeKeySchema = 1`; old source-edge runs with `key_schema = 0` fail closed.
A `CondemnedRow` stores `delete_pending`, the full `Token`, `size`, and `condemn_round`; `encodeCondemnedRow` uses `[0x02][flags][token_type][round][size][len][value]`.
`openSourceEdgeRun` validates `RunKind::SourceEdge` and `key_schema == kSourceEdgeKeySchema`, and `assertValidSourceEdgeId` reserves `UInt128{0}` for the condemned sentinel namespace.

`CondemnedSummary` contains `condemned_total`, `pending_total`, and `oldest_nonpending_condemn_round`, with `UINT64_MAX` meaning no nonpending condemned row; the protobuf field is `repeated CondemnedSummaryProto condemned_summary = 7`.

`kCondemned` persists the full token type: `ETag = 1`, `Generation = 2`, and `Emulated = 3`; decoding fails with `CORRUPTED_DATA` for an unknown `token_type` or a payload length inconsistent with `token_len`.
`source_id = 0` is reserved for sentinel rows: `sourceEdgeId` must throw `LOGICAL_ERROR` on a zero result and delta producers must reject `source_id == 0`.

`SourceEdgeKeyCodec` derives digest length from the algorithm byte, rejects unknown algorithms with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, and rejects a known algorithm with the wrong total key length using `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
The `hash_algo` envelope field records the blob's `BlobHashAlgo`; it is a defensive consistency check, while `PoolMeta` and the path segment are authoritative.
`HashingWriteBuffer` checksums for run files and manifests remain `cityHash128`; only the blob content address is selectable.
The Phase 2 digest representation is `BlobDigest` with `std::array<uint8_t,32>` bytes, big-endian ordering, and zero-filled tail bytes beyond the pool's meaningful digest length.
Only the content digest widens for SHA-256; `payload_digest`, `RunRef.checksum`, `sourceEdgeId`, lease owners, heartbeat owners, and `manifestCleanupShard` remain `UInt128` internal identifiers.
S3 staging promotion must use `If-None-Match:*` on `CopyObject` and on `CompleteMultipartUpload`; unconditional overwrite is forbidden.

The Native CAS backend exposes `supportsConditionalCopy()`, `stageStream(staging_key)`, and `promoteStaged(staging_key, blob_key)`; Local and Emulated backends report unsupported and use local staging.

The mixed-algorithm implementation retypes `BlobDelta`, `BlobCandidate`, `RetiredEntry`, `OutcomeEntry`, `.meta` APIs, dedup-cache keys, and pending dependencies to `BlobRef` rather than retaining digest-only identity overloads.
The Phase 2 digest codec must reject wrong-width hex or byte input with `BAD_ARGUMENTS` and assert that tail bytes beyond a 16-byte pool digest are zero.

The S3 staging plan requires `ConditionalCopyResult{created, dest_etag}` and makes unsupported conditional copy throw or select local staging rather than provide a non-enforcing default implementation.
A CAS-owned S3 retry controller is required for the ref protocol and provides single-attempt conditional writes, exact-key resolution, and lease gating.

Conditional `If-None-Match` and `If-Match` CAS writes perform exactly one HTTP attempt, using a request-scoped override so unrelated S3 disks retain their retry configuration. The underlying S3 client performs exactly one HTTP attempt for `If-None-Match` and `If-Match` writes, and a process-wide retry-count change is unacceptable if it alters unrelated S3 workloads. SDK-level retries must remain zero for conditional writes, and tests assert exact request counts so an invisible SDK retry fails the test.

Raw conditional-write results classify as `Committed` for 2xx, `DefiniteFailure` only for whitelisted malformed-request, entity-too-large, or access-denied classes, and `Unresolved` for timeout, connection loss, 5xx, or unresolved `PreconditionFailed`; `PreconditionFailed` is never a definite failure.
`CasRequestController::putIfAbsentControlled` performs put-if-absent with resolve-before-reissue and checks the fence before every attempt and before returning `Committed`.
Ref wire messages use fixed-width little-endian integers and u32-length-prefixed byte strings, begin with `u32 format_version = 1`, and fail closed on unknown versions.

Read-only exact `GET` and `HEAD` operations use CAS-bounded retries, paginated `LIST` resumes only with its returned continuation token, immutable conditional creates resolve by exact-key observation, and exact deletes never broaden their target.

A run-file block CRC must cover the block head, including `record_count`, `min_key`, and `max_key`, as well as the payload; `RunFileReader::next` must use bounds-checked decoding and require exact block consumption.
`decodeFoldSeal` must reject `TokenType` values outside `ETag`, `Generation`, and `Emulated`, and `RefNsCleanupState` values outside `Pending` and `Completed`, with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

`Expect: 100-continue` negotiation is scoped to CAS-owned conditional writes using `WriteSettings::s3_conditional_write_use_expect_continue`, which defaults to `false`; non-CAS conditional writes such as Iceberg `If-None-Match` retain historical wire behavior.

A dedup-cache hit does not skip the occupancy `HEAD`; it selects the `head_first` branch, and the `HEAD` runs precisely on hits, while the avoided operation is the body PUT counted by `CasBlobBodyPutAvoided`.
CAS v3 fixes JSON keys to 2–5 characters, uses full-word values, and requires units to be recorded in the registry; per-object field tables are implementation-plan work under those conventions.

Every v3 CAS object has a header line `{"type":"cas_<object>","v":N}` with `v` as the only version field and gated before the body; the body is a control JSON object, sorted NDJSON records, or a raw payload zone, with a trailer for line-structured bodies.
CAS codecs use streaming `ReadHelpers`/`WriteHelpers` JSON primitives over `ReadBuffer` and hand-written deterministic writers; they do not use a DOM library.

Compression is a deterministic per-type policy of `Never`, `Always`, or `PinnedRaw` with no size threshold; `cas_ref_log`, `cas_ref_snap`, `cas_part_manifest`, and `cas_gc_outcomes` are always compressed under a `.zst` key suffix, while `cas_run` and `cas_fold_seal` remain raw. The deterministic formats `cas_run` and `cas_fold_seal` are `PinnedRaw` and `Strict`, while the Always-compressed set is exactly `cas_ref_log`, `cas_ref_snap`, `cas_part_manifest`, and `cas_gc_outcomes`, whose `storedSuffix` is `.zst`.

Additive CAS format evolution uses a new tolerant key, while breaking evolution requires a `v` bump, `G_BUILD`/`changePoints`, and write-down-to-floor; deterministic formats use strict keys and the adoption pin to re-encode at the existing object's version on a `putDeterministicArtifact` conflict.
The optional provider-metadata mirror sets `Content-Type` per object family and `x-amz-meta-cas` to a copy of the CAS header line; the protocol never reads this metadata.

The settled `cas_blob` header fields are `type`, `v`, `tag`, `bld`, `ts`, `by`, `op`, `ch`, and truncated `ref`; `hash_algo`, `domain_id`, `header_hash`, and `writer_version` are dropped, and the header is padded to byte 255 plus `
` while `blob_header_len` remains 256.

`Core/Formats/` may include only IO primitives and identifier vocabulary such as `CasIds`, `CasToken`, `CasBlobRef`, `CasManifestId`, `CasRefIds`, and `CasBlobDigest`; it must not include `CasBackend`, `CasStore`, or subsystem headers.

Adding a persisted CAS object requires one `FormatId` and traits-table row, one `Cas<Object>Format.{h,cpp}` containing the wire struct, codec, and invariants, one documented `CasLayout` key builder, one shared-test registration, and one same-commit `Formats/README.md` row.

Phase-1 files in `Core/Formats/` are physically restricted to format headers, identifier vocabulary, base, IO, Common, format settings, and zstd dependencies; they must not include `CasBackend.h`, `CasStore.h`, or subsystem headers.

Phase-1 canonical text writers emit no whitespace outside JSON strings and terminate every line with `
`; hashes and ids are lowercase fixed-width hex strings, unbounded `u64` values are decimal strings, and bounded counts, lengths, and millisecond timestamps are JSON numbers.
`writeHeaderLine` stamps `currentCompatibilityVersion`, which equals `G_BUILD` and is 3; the `G_BUILD` 3-to-4 bump belongs to phase 2 rather than phase 1.

Phase 1 freezes `FormatId::RefLog = 19`, `FormatId::RefSnapshot = 20`, `FormatId::BlobMeta = 21`, and `FormatId::GcHeartbeat = 22`; each receives a `BASELINE` change-point ladder and none receives a legacy binary magic.

The phase-1 traits registry provides `traitsFor`, `traitsForType`, and `storedSuffix` over `TextFamily`, `KeyStrictness`, and `CompressionPolicy`, with an object cap and line cap for every non-reserved format; `FormatId::Roster` is reserved and has no traits.

`JsonObjectReader` is a pull cursor for one canonical JSON object: `nextKey` rejects duplicate keys, `readHex128` requires exactly 32 lowercase hex characters, and `skipUnknown` rejects `!` keys with `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`, rejects unknown keys in strict formats with `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and skips unknown keys in tolerant formats.

`CasTextFormat` exposes `writeHeaderLine`, `writeTrailerLine`, `expectHeaderLine`, `sniffHeaderLine`, and `readLine`; `expectHeaderLine` validates type and compatibility without swallowing errors, while `sniffHeaderLine` returns no value for non-CAS or malformed input for fsck and dispatch.

`sealObject` compresses only `Always` formats into one zstd frame, and `openObject` accepts raw bodies but accepts compressed input only for `Always` formats, checking the declared decompressed size against the cap before allocating output.
Phase 2 keeps `G_BUILD = 3` and adds no `changePoints` entry because it introduces no breaking text-format generation; future breaking changes earn the version bump.
CAS JSON writing pins `FormatSettings::JSON::escape_forward_slashes` to false, so slash characters remain unescaped and text bytes do not depend on ClickHouse-wide defaults.

Phase-2 JSON encodes enum values as full words, hashes and UUIDs as 32-character lowercase hex strings, unbounded counters as decimal strings, bounded integers as JSON numbers, and `UINT64_MAX` sentinel fields as decimal strings.
The shared `CasWireVocab` renders `Token` as sibling keys `tt` and `tv`, `BlobRef` as sibling keys `ha` and `h`, and maps token, blob-hash, and object-kind enums through fail-closed word maps.
`PoolMeta::blob_header_len` must be at least 96, a multiple of 8, and at most 16384; `algos_used` must be non-empty, strictly increasing, and contain only valid `BlobHashAlgo` values.
Both refsnaplog formats belong to the `Control` family with `Tolerant` keys, `Always`/`.zst` storage, `object_cap = 64 MiB`, and `line_cap = 64 KiB`.
Refsnaplog text headers stamp `v = G_BUILD = 3`; this migration does not bump `G_BUILD` or append a `changePoints` entry.
The `cas_ref_log` text shape is a `cas_ref_log` header, a meta line containing `ns`, `we`, and `rs`, one record line per `RefOp`, and a `{"n":count}` trailer.
The `cas_ref_snap` text shape is a `cas_ref_snap` header, a meta line containing lifecycle and optional removal/seal fields, committed and precommit record lines, and a `{"n":count}` trailer.
Refsnaplog text uses `we`/`rs` for the primary `RefTxnId`, `rte`/`rts` for `remove_txn_id`, `sfe`/`sfs` for `sealed_from`, and `me`/`mb`/`mo` for `ManifestRef` fields.
`cas_blob_meta` is a three-scalar `Control` object containing `state`, `condemn_round`, and `size`, converted from the fixed 22-byte `CAMT` binary codec to one-line JSON text.
Blob-meta JSON encodes `state` as `clean` or `condemned` and encodes `condemn_round` and `size` as decimal strings.
`BlobMeta.version` remains in the in-memory struct with default value `1` for `CasInspect`, but is not serialized because the header `v` is the authoritative format version.

`loadMeta`, `putMetaIfAbsent`, `casMeta`, and `deleteMetaExact` remain in `Core/CasBlobMeta` while `MetaState`, `BlobMeta`, `encodeBlobMeta`, and `decodeBlobMeta` move to `Core/Formats/CasBlobMetaFormat`.
Blob-meta text stamps `v = G_BUILD = 3` without adding a new format generation or `changePoints` entry.
The record-stream codec is backend-free and operates on caller-owned `ReadBuffer` and `WriteBuffer`; backend stream ownership stays in `Core/CasBlobInDegree`.
A source-edge record maps to JSON keys `b` for the algo-prefixed lowercase blob reference, `s` for a 32-character lowercase-hex source ID, and `m` for `edge`, `zero`, or `condemned`.

Each inline manifest entry is represented by an `il` length in its JSON record, while its arbitrary bytes are stored after the trailer as a banner line, exactly `il` raw bytes, and a newline; EOF must follow the last segment.

`encodePartManifest` returns canonical uncompressed text for text-size budgeting; backend PUTs seal that text, backend GETs open it before decoding, and exchange remains text-to-text without wrapping.
Part-manifest text stamps `v = G_BUILD = 3`, drops the binary `writer_version`, uses `Tolerant` JSON keys and `Always`/`.zst`, and has no dual-read path.
The blob envelope is a fixed-length 256-byte JSON header: a JSON object, ASCII-space padding, and a newline at byte 255, with the payload beginning at the header length.
The envelope's ref budget is `(L - 1) - PREFIX.size() - SUFFIX.size()`, with `L` equal to the pool's `blob_header_len`; the ref is incrementally escaped and truncated without splitting an escape.
Envelope JSON maps `tag`, `bld`, and `by` to 32-character lowercase hex strings, `ts` and `ch` to JSON numbers, `op` to a full word, and `ref` to the locally escaped diagnostic string.
The envelope drops `hash_algo`, `domain_id`, `header_hash`, and `writer_version`; `CityHash64` is no longer part of envelope processing.
The envelope header is built before payload streaming, so header construction has no payload dependency and remains compatible with S3-native staging.
After codecs v3, `Formats/` contains per-object format files and includes only IO primitives and identifier vocabulary, never `CasBackend.h` or subsystem headers.

The CA in-commit upload-retry stack is caller-agnostic: INSERT and MERGE share `putBlob`, `uploadFromSource`, and `CasRequestController`, and both keep the staged scratch temporary alive across retries.

`CasRequestControl` uses a 16-attempt, 90-second default operation budget, while `putBlob` has an outer eight-round loop that catches only `ABORTED`; deterministic local failures are rethrown immediately.
The S36 dedup-on-TO-CA check uses deterministic `repeat('cas-move-dedup-probe-', 100)` payloads so a second move of byte-identical content must observe `CasBlobPutDedup > 0` and `CasBlobPut == 0`.
Review finding №3 is refuted because `HEAD` precedes `GET`; a mixed result can contain newer bytes with an older token, and conditional consumers fail closed on that stale-token combination.

The controlled CAS body-upload path classifies 5xx and 429 conditional-write results as `Unresolved`, resolves them by HEAD, and retries within `attempt_timeout_ms=5000`, `operation_deadline_ms=90000`, and `max_attempts=16` with capped-exponential backoff.

`CasJsonWriter` is intended to replace `WriteBuffer` in all CAS text-format encode paths while preserving byte-identical output; the read side, `JsonObjectReader`, `src/IO/WriteHelpers.h`, and every on-wire byte remain unchanged.
The CAS string writer must be the single escaping path for all strings and must not offer a trust-based raw-string shortcut; its semantics are fixed to `escape_forward_slashes = false`.
The `RecordStream` family, including `cas_run`, must remain streaming and bounded by one line (`line_cap` 4 KiB), never by record count.

The `cas_run` writer assembles each NDJSON line in one reused `CasJsonWriter`, performs one bulk `WriteBuffer::write` per line, then calls `clear()` so capacity is retained and memory stays bounded by the largest line.
Decoded interserver `ManifestEntry.path` values must be relative and contain no empty, `.` or `..` path segments; legal projection subdirectories remain valid.
`S3ObjectStorage` owns a lazily built single-attempt client clone and must rebuild it when the disk client rotates, while CAS conditional writes select `ObjectStorageRetryProfile::SingleAttempt`.
Non-S3 backends may ignore `ObjectStorageRetryProfile::SingleAttempt`; only CAS sets the profile today and an unsupported backend need not throw at profile-selection time.

The dedicated CAS upload pool is disjoint from `getThreadPoolWriter`, and its getter fails loudly when uninitialized or when the configured pool size is zero. Blob fan-out uses a dedicated server-wide pool disjoint from `getThreadPoolWriter`; the caller only submits and joins, pool size 1 is valid and serializes work, the getter fails if uninitialized, and a configured size of 0 is rejected.
In the phased engine, a per-part manifest edge is durably precommitted before any of that part's blobs are uploaded, and promote runs only after all of that part's blobs are complete.

`Cas::PartWriteTxn::uploadBlobDetached` must not read or mutate `PartWriteTxn` `build` state, because the transaction is single-writer; it returns a `BlobUploadResult` containing the complete dependency effect and outcome.

Condemned-local resurrection uses a byte-weighted semaphore whose weight is the checked header-plus-payload size; a blob heavier than total capacity gets exclusive access after the semaphore drains, and the permit is released after `putOverwrite` and body destruction.
Blob fan-out groups pending blobs by `BlobRef`, rejects conflicting declared sizes, launches exactly one task per unique ref, and merges exactly one dependency result per unique ref.

`BlobUploadRequest` is a public CAS-owned type containing `BlobRef`, a source descriptor, and `declared_size`; `BlobUploadResult` contains `BlobRef`, the complete `BlobDepRecord`, and one of seven upload outcomes.
Publish-confirm uses protocol version 11 with `content_addressed_confirm` as the confirm action parameter and `content_addressed_source_token` as the relink-offer response cookie.
The removed snapshot/ref-log field `pl` is explicitly rejected in both former wire locations, including negative decoding tests, rather than silently ignored.

`HoleyListBackend` omits one chosen durable key from one qualifying `list` call while leaving exact `get` and `head` for that key functional, modeling an incomplete enumeration without modeling a particular pagination mechanism.

A fail-closed read-only `Backend` decorator should make every `put*` and `delete*` operation throw `READONLY`; `ca-gc-rebuild`'s single `gc/state` CAS must be an explicit exception rather than an accidental hole.

The observed hole firing was not explained by a phantom key, concurrent ref-object deletion, stale-epoch minting, out-of-order appends, late landing, page-limit mismatch, or different key filters: the hole keys were `HEAD`-present, there were zero ref-object deletes in the relevant minute, all 65,263 uploads were ordered by writer epoch, and both walks used limit 1000 and `parseRefObjectKey`.

At firing time, `HEAD` distinguishes the two opposite enumeration defects: `present` means a durable object was omitted by an enumeration, while `absent` means the other enumeration returned a nonexistent key and indicts the client or iterator; this distinction cannot be recovered after legitimate deletion.
The HEAD-before-GET pair is a standing-veto protocol step; its cost is measured as the number of edges multiplied by approximately 0.9 ms per round trip, without proposing removal.
An `EpochSeal` transaction contains exactly one seal operation; `prev_epoch_seal` is required on sequence 1 of every non-genesis epoch, including an empty epoch, and is forbidden elsewhere.

Stage A's `EpochSeal` grammar requires exactly one `EpochSeal` operation, requires `prev_epoch_seal` at sequence 1 when `writer_epoch > life_epoch`, and forbids it at genesis `{life_epoch, 1}` and elsewhere.

`slotOccupy` performs exactly one conditional create and, only on conflict resolution, one raw exact GET; it never lists, never retries internally, and returns `Created`, `Occupied` with occupant bytes/token, or `Unresolved`.

Fold-seal decoding rejects classifications outside `{0,1,2,4}` before narrowing, rejects classification-4 holds with zero `offending_position`, and rejects duplicate `(namespace, shard)` coverage rows; encoders reject the same malformed shapes.

Within one `putIfAbsentControlled` call, `DefiniteFailure` is reported only when every attempt is definite; any earlier unresolved ambiguous attempt dominates the call verdict and preserves `ApplyPending`.
Blob re-hashing establishes content identity, `HEAD`-before-`PUT` is the deduplication admission gate, and a condemned object is never revived by reading it back; revival requires a fresh upload.
The S3 conditional-write policy treats HTTP 412 as deterministic and non-retryable, exposed through `S3Exception::isPreconditionFailed` and `RetryStrategy`.

Identifiers belonging to compare-and-swap rather than the CAS feature are excluded from naming changes, including `casPut`, `CasOutcome`, `CasResult`, `CasOp::Cas`, `CasOp::CasConflict`, and the `CasRequestControl.h` family.

During the incident, exact-key `GET` and `HEAD` remained truthful while LIST was not, and conditional writes were trusted because `putIfAbsent` cannot report `Created` over an existing key without data loss.

`CasRequestController` provides single-attempt conditional writes, a budget, fence gating, and exact-key resolution for the ref lane, but `promoteStaged`'s `copyObjectConditional` is a separate retry mechanism and `casPutObject`/`casRemoveObject` still use the disk default retry policy.
`casPutObject` retries with the same frozen payload after a token conflict, so a future concurrent appender requires a real `casAppendObject` that re-reads base content inside the retry loop.

The `EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE` writer order is body, `precommitAdd`, `putBlob`, then `promote`; it makes the precommit closure edge durable before blob adoption and is relied on by the two-phase GC deletion recheck.
`ObjectStorageBackend::get` maps NoSuchKey/HTTP 404 to `std::nullopt`, allowing a legitimate live read in a HEAD-to-GET deletion window to surface cleanly instead of exposing raw Code 499.

`supportsListTokens()` and `tokenForList` expose a LIST-derived incarnation token only for the blob-condemn exact-delete-versus-`HEAD` decision, never for skipping a manifest or owner-transition fold read.
Once a successor's `SealSlot` occupies the key, `WedgeRetryOccupied` must reject the retry regardless of the presented generation; the seal is conclusive during the pre-seal race.
Ref-log ids are per-namespace contiguous ids derived from state, and an id whose create outcome is ambiguous must not be reused under the every-attempt rule.
Every ref-log write is a create-if-absent operation; an unconditional PUT must not overwrite an epoch seal.

A namespace inactive while global writer epochs advance must close every skipped epoch in order with an empty sequence-1 `EpochSeal` before its later consumer can authorize recovery, fold, or destruction.
`Cas::Store` already exposes the protocol primitives `resolveRef`, `readManifest`, `locate`, `dropRef`, `updateRefPublishedAt`, and `dropNamespace` needed by the cache facade.
`Cas::Backend` is the token-aware storage seam used by `Store`, `Build`, `Gc`, liveness keepers, capability probing, and fsck; its load-bearing contract is the token-to-content precondition.
In `system.cas_log`, `object_hash` is lowercase hex and `token` is the involved incarnation `ETag` when applicable.
Blob objects are stored at <prefix>/blobs/<first-two-hex-chars>/<32-hex-blob-id>, produced by Layout::blobKey
decodeEnvelopeHeader validates CABL magic, compatibility_version, critical extensions, header length, object-size arithmetic, and header_hash
Persisted token values remain opaque strings and token_type, rather than provider-specific string shape, determines whether a token is ETag, generation, or emulated

The v3 cas_blob header occupies exactly 256 bytes: JSON occupies [0,json_len), spaces occupy [json_len,255), and byte 255 is a newline Additionally, The v3 cas_blob envelope retains constant payload offset blob_header_len = 256 and does not use frame-level compression because payload identity is the raw bytes
The v3 cas_blob tag is a fresh random u128 per upload attempt and is the exact-token delete primitive; bld attributes newborn debris to the writer build
Provider metadata is only a mirror for eyes and dashboards; the CAS protocol never reads it and must fail closed if it is absent
RustFS has demonstrably returned incomplete LIST results, while AWS S3 was untested in the cited investigation; correctness cannot rely on assumed store LIST behavior.
Freshness metadata is advisory: writers may point-read per-hash `.meta`, but reads do not consult it, GC deletes the blob body first, and an absent meta is equivalent to `Clean`.
Mutable and control protobuf objects should use `CasHeader`; streamed blob payloads should keep a binary envelope, and GC data-plane runs should use `RunFile`.
CAS blobs and manifests are immutable, content-addressed, write-once objects, and GC is required to preserve no dangle, no returned token, and over-count rather than under-count.
Persisted `BlobRef` fields use `ha` for the hash algorithm and `h` for the digest hex, and the searched user-facing tools contain no `p` JSON/output key.
Setting `metadata_type` to `cas` makes an object-storage disk content-addressed, shares identical content across parts or tables, and enables background reclamation after references disappear.
CAS integration configs use `<metadata_type>cas</metadata_type>` and the relink test asserts the wire literals `cas_pool_uuid`, `cas_relink=part_manifest_v2`, and `cas_source_token`.
`uploadPendingBlobs` creates one `Cas::BlobUploadRequest` per referenced pending blob and delegates to the free function `DB::Cas::fanOutBlobUploads(build, requests, pool, hooks=nullptr)`.

Fan-out tasks write only their own pre-sized stable result slot; the runner is declared after the result vector so its destructor drains every task before the vector is destroyed, including a dispatch-loop throw (`B90`).
`waitForAllToFinishAndRethrowFirstError` drains all tasks and then rethrows the first failure in ascending-ref order, and a rethrow bypasses merging results.
Duplicate blob references collapse to one upload task, and conflicting duplicate declared sizes are rejected with `LOGICAL_ERROR`.
Fan-out concurrency is bounded by the supplied pool size: pool 2 reaches peak concurrency 2, while pool 1 degenerates to serial execution with a bounded wait.
`clickhouse-local` initializes the blob-upload pool from `content_addressed_blob_upload_pool_size` during `LocalServer::initialize` and shuts it down during `LocalServer::cleanup`.
`clickhouse-disks` initializes the blob-upload pool with `DB::Cas::initializeBlobUploadPool(16)` and shuts it down in its existing `SCOPE_EXIT_SAFE` block.

The generation-8 canonical snapshot wire remains byte-identical, retains mandatory `"lc":"live"`, and does not bump `G_BUILD`. Additionally, The generation-8 snapshot byte golden still begins with `{"type":"cas_ref_snap","v":8}` and retains the same ordered `"lc":"live"` metadata field.

Snapshot encoding writes literal `lc = live`; decoding requires the `lc` field and accepts exactly `live`. Additionally, `writeSnapshotMeta` writes `live`, `decodeRefTableSnapshot` requires `lc`, and decoding rejects every `lc` value other than `live`.
Generation-8 snapshot decoding explicitly rejects retired `rte` alone, `rts` alone, and `rte` plus `rts` instead of skipping them as unknown fields.
`snapshotFramingSize` takes only `(ns, snapshot_id, row_count)` and preserves its exact byte count.
`src/Disks/tests/gtest_cas_fold_seal_format.cpp:318` intentionally constructs the generation-6 `nsc` record and requires the generation-7 decoder to reject the marker-driven handshake.
The HEAD-before-GET pair is a protocol step and must not be removed as a cheap performance optimization.
HTTP 412 `Precondition Failed` is deterministic for conditional requests and must not be retried, even when an SDK classifies a non-AWS error body as retryable `UNKNOWN`.

The GCS conditional dialect maps `If-None-Match: *` to `x-goog-if-generation-match: 0`, maps numeric `If-Match` to `x-goog-if-generation-match: <generation>`, rejects non-numeric `If-Match`, and rejects conditional `CompleteMultipartUpload`. Additionally, GCS XML API conditional writes require native GOOG4 signing and `x-goog-if-generation-match`; AWS `If-Match`/`If-None-Match` and SigV4 semantics are insufficient, and GCS may ignore conditional multipart completion.

The object-storage interface provides `removeObjectIfTokenMatches` for token-exact deletion and `copyObjectConditional` for write-once server-side copy with `If-None-Match: *`, both with fail-closed defaults.
`conditionalOpsUseGenerationTokens` and `isBucketVersioningEnabled` expose GCS generation-token and versioned-bucket capabilities so conditional operations can fail closed when unsupported.

`WriteBufferFromFileBase` exposes `getResultObjectETag`, and `WriteBufferFromFileDecorator` forwards it so a CAS writer can record the written incarnation token without a follow-up HEAD request. Additionally, The ETag fix makes `WriteBufferFromS3` return the `PutObject` or `CompleteMultipartUpload` response ETag, eliminating the head-after-put `HEAD`.

A blob's identity H is a streaming, chunked cityHash128 computed incrementally via HashingWriteBuffer with block size DBMS_DEFAULT_HASHING_BLOCK_SIZE = 2048 as bytes are written, not a one-shot hash of a pre-existing buffer and not read from checksums.txt; the storage key is blobs/<H[:2]>/<H>.

Upload by placement: new content is written PUT If-None-Match:* (idempotent, dedup hit skips upload); cold reuse of an existing blob point-reads the object's per-hash .meta freshness state (Core/CasBlobMeta.h, MetaState{Clean,Condemned}) — condemned triggers resurrect with a fresh incarnation_tag, else the blob is reused as-is; this point-read replaced the old writer-side retire view.

The build writes a precommit binding to a /_precommits namespace shard before publish, giving GC visibility into in-flight blobs; the fold barrier holds the +1 edge until the manifest body is present. Publish is one CAS PUT to the ref shard updating refs[part_name] and appending {+, name, T} to the journal atomically; tokened deps are edge-protected (EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE) and not re-checked at promote, while non-tokened deps get a per-hash .meta point-read and copy-forward-if-condemned inline in the blob-revalidation loop.

CAS's condemned detection is a per-hash `.meta` point-read (`BlobMeta{version, state, condemn_round, size}` with `MetaState::Clean`/`Condemned`), not a writer-side retired-view cache; the earlier `Store::syncRetiredView`/`observed_gc_round`/`view_gate` machinery and the `MountLease.observed_gc_round` field are removed entirely. GC always writes a `Condemned` meta before ever deleting the body, so an absent meta reads exactly as live as a `Clean` one.

The writer consults the per-hash `.meta` with a single GET (`loadMeta`) only at `Build::observeAndAdmit` (dedup-hit/adopt path) and `Build::uploadFromSource` (fresh-upload/condemned-displacement path); a `Clean` or absent meta is adopted for free, a `Condemned` meta throws `ABORTED` so the caller re-uploads from source (INV-1) rather than reading the dying object.

EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE manifest-trust adoption: for a tokenless W-EVIDENCE dependency naming a blob referenced by a live committed source manifest, `Build::promote` trusts the durable manifest edge (`isTrustedAdopt`) with NO per-file HEAD/GET, because the source pins the blob (in-degree >= 1, GC cannot condemn it) and this build's own precommit edge is re-proved live at the promote owner-liveness gate before the trust fires; `copyForwardFromCondemned`/`isCopyForwardableTokenless` are deleted as a result.

On GCS's S3-compatible XML surface signed with sigv4, none of the conditional operations CAS needs are enforced (create-if-absent, conditional overwrite, and conditional delete are all silently ignored — a wrong-ETag DELETE on GCS S3-compat actually deletes the object); the same HMAC credential pair, signed instead with GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256 over the GCS XML endpoint, enforces all of them via `x-goog-if-generation-match`.

The pluggable blob-hash Phase 1 design encodes the hash algorithm identifier directly in the blob's storage path (`blobs/<algo>/<shard>/<hex>`), records the pool's chosen algorithm in `PoolMeta`, and fail-close-validates that recorded algorithm against the disk's configured algorithm on every open, so an existing pool is never silently re-hashed under a different algorithm.

The content-hash algorithm (CityHash128) is an unversioned, unpinned pool contract (AD1-3): a future change to the hash algorithm would silently fork dedup and break relink, because nothing pins or versions which hash algorithm a pool's content-addressed keys were computed with.

`CasEnvelope` is a 70-byte little-endian core header (magic, writer_version, compatibility_version, hash_algo, flags, header_len, domain_id[16], incarnation_tag[16], build_id[16], header_hash[8]) followed by TLV extensions padded to a per-pool fixed `header_len`, so blob payloads always start at a constant offset for a constant-shift `locate`; `logical_size`/`logical_hash` core fields were dropped 2026-07-11 to let the header be built before the payload streams (S3-native staging).

`CasBlobMeta` (the `.meta` freshness sibling) is a fixed `CAMT`-magic codec with `BODY_LEN=22` (magic[4]+version[1]+state[1]+condemn_round[8 LE]+size[8 LE]); `version` must equal 1 and `state` must be Clean=0 or Condemned=1, else decode fail-closes.
Plain dedup adoption itself is free of `.meta` write cost (`CasBuild.cpp:337`); an earlier revision of the soak audit mislabeled the dedup-adoption class as carrying `.meta` write tags.

The envelope's `domain_id`, `incarnation_tag`, and `build_id` are excluded from `logical_hash`, allowing a new physical incarnation without changing the content address. Additionally, The incarnation tag is carried in the object body rather than provider metadata so changing it creates a new backend token without a metadata copy and remains portable across S3, GCS, and Azure. Additionally, Incarnation identity is stored in the object body rather than provider metadata because metadata is write-once and requires copy operations, has an 8 KiB cap, and S3 ETags identify content rather than metadata.

For tokenless evidence dependencies, `observeAndAdmit` reads and verifies the condemned object, wraps the payload with a fresh `incarnation_tag` and this build's `build_id`, and conditionally overwrites the observed token before admitting the new token.

Condemned-blob recreation uses the existing `Build::putBlob` cold-reuse rule on a retried build; the promote gate remains fail-closed with `ABORTED` because build-local sources are not retained at promote time.
GCS conditional semantics require a non-`x-amz` authentication dialect: GOOG4-HMAC or OAuth Bearer; `x-goog-*` headers cannot be mixed into sigv4 requests because GCS returns `ExcessHeaderValues`.

Build retains a parallel map of BlobSource objects for every putBlob hash, including streamed uploads and dedup-adopted blobs, because DepEntry is reassigned on adopt paths. Additionally, The tokened fix retains BlobSource in a parallel map for every putBlob hash, including dedup-adopted hashes, because later condemnation can affect an adopted incarnation too.
Build::promote keeps the outside-the-lock tokenless copy-forward pre-pass as a fast path and adds an in-closure backstop for condemnations visible only in the refreshed view.
The settled v3 blob layout keeps one key per hash and a minimal in-body 16-byte incarnation_tag plus payload; the manifest remains pure content and reads use a constant offset.
Freshness-meta v3 replaces writer-side RetireView retired-list downloads with per-hash .meta point-reads while leaving the exact-token body-delete core and read path unchanged.

An HTTP-attempt timeout is not the deadline for a complete logical CAS operation; CAS code owns retries, gates attempts on the local mount fence and remaining lease time, resolves uncertain writes from exact keys where permitted, and bounds retry budgets.
No protocol-significant CAS operation inherits an unexamined generic S3 retry policy.
Object-storage token handling is consolidated into `tokenForHead`, `tokenForList`, and `tokenMatches` so native ETag, GCS generation, and emulated list-token policies have one source of truth.

The shared S3 412 policy is consolidated into `S3::isPreconditionFailedError` and `S3Exception::isPreconditionFailed`, checking the HTTP response code first and canonical exception name/message as fallback.

Insert and merge uploads have different recovery behavior under a RustFS stall: an insert can re-stream from its still-live scratch file inside the query, while a merge failure discards the whole task and rebuilds without a durable object to adopt; proposed remedies are preserving staged merge results or using a size-proportional stream budget, with a circuit breaker as the outer safety limit.
Every persisted CAS format is converted to text, including `ref_log`, `ref_snap`, and the `blob_meta` sidecar; raw payload bytes are the only binary exception.
Wire structs such as `BlobMeta`, `RefLogTxn`, and `FoldSeal` move with their codecs into `Core/Formats/`, while protocol logic requiring a backend or layout remains in `Core/`.
`RefOwnerBinding` and `RefOwnerKind` are shared by the ref log and snapshot codecs in `Core/Formats/CasRefWireVocab.{h,cpp}` so peer codecs do not depend on one another.

The part manifest remains one object; its embedded `CARN` `RunKind::ManifestEntries` stream is replaced inside the same body by JSON entry lines and a trailer, with no separate object and no `CasRecordStreamFormat` reuse.
`ObjectKind`, `ProvenanceOp`, `Provenance`, and the slim `EnvelopeHeader` move with the envelope codec into `Core/Formats/CasBlobEnvelopeFormat`, while `CasEnvelope.{h,cpp}` are deleted.

The proposed `CasBlobUploader` extraction moves byte delivery such as `putBlob`, `observeAndAdmit`, `uploadFromSource`, HEAD-first handling, and staging promote/resurrect execution, while admit/adopt/resurrect choice, dependency recording, and the `promote` gate remain transaction state.

The CA branch of `DataPartStorageOnDiskBase::clonePart` creates one destination transaction, recursively streams every source file through non-autocommit `IDiskTransaction::writeFile`, and commits once. Additionally, The L2 fix copies every part file sequentially through one destination CA transaction and commits once, causing `publishStaging` and `PartWriteTxn` to upload deduplicated blobs, create one manifest, and publish one ref atomically.
Cross-disk CA part copying is sequential because the transaction's staging map is not mutex-guarded and MOVE is latency-insensitive; parallel copying is deferred optimization work.

Freshness-meta conditional writes must be routed through the shared `CasRequestController`, using controlled put-if-absent and controlled If-Match overwrite variants; transient errors must be absorbed inside the controlled call rather than swallowed as best-effort failures because stale meta state affects point readers.

Transient CAS write failures that are rerouted to the client use `NETWORK_ERROR` and a retry-later path, while terminal content conflicts such as `republishRef`'s unique-reference refusal remain `ABORTED`.

`CasJsonWriter` owns a `String`, appends inline, and supports whole-object assembly for bounded formats plus a reused line-scratch mode for streaming formats; it avoids `WriteBuffer` lifecycle overhead and per-record heap allocations.

`CasJsonWriter::stringValue` scans for control bytes, quotes, backslashes, and `0xE2`, bulk-appends safe runs, and preserves the canonical JSON escaping for `\b`, `\f`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\u00XX`, U+2028, U+2029, partial `0xE2` sequences, and unescaped `/`.
Per-write retry behavior is selected with the backend-neutral `ObjectStorageRetryProfile` token, whose values are `Default` and `SingleAttempt`.

The CAS-specific predicates `isMalformedRequestError`, `isEntityTooLargeError`, and `isAccessDeniedError` are moved to `S3Common` so CAS classification and `S3Exception::isRetryableError` share maintained error-name lists; `isRetryableError` itself is not changed.

`PartWriteTxn::uploadBlobDetached` is a side-effect-free upload primitive that returns value-only results and does not mutate transaction state; upload results are merged into each part's build serially after the join.
`RefOp::payload` and the related `RefPayloadUpdate` API are deleted under the pre-release no-compatibility policy; `SetPayload` becomes `SetPublishedAt` with wire word `set_published_at`.
The multi-commit design uses one dedicated CAS upload pool disjoint from `getThreadPoolWriter`; upload tasks return `DepEntry` values and merge them into `build->deps` only after joining.

`uploadBlobDetached` keeps conditional body/meta operations, freshness transition to `Clean`, condemned-object resurrection, dedup-cache operations, event emission, request accounting, and ProfileEvents inside each upload task so branch ordering is preserved.

The validator uses fixed 128-bit `XXH3_128` through `Primitives/CasXxh3Streamer.h`, not the pool's pluggable `blob_hash`, because it is a protocol validator that must compare consistently across disks.
Content-addressed encryption deduplication is scoped per encryption key, with key-local hash derivation.

The proposed `ch128ctx` blob hash is `cityHash128(content) ∥ xxh3_64(part_name, file_name) ∥ size`, a 256-bit slot-bound digest intended to prevent cross-slot adversarial deduplication while preserving same-slot retry and replica-write deduplication.

`Build::putBlob` was changed to stream the staged source instead of materializing it in a `String`, resolving the observed CA upload memory blow-up. Additionally, Before the streaming fix, `Build::putBlob` could materialize a `BlobSource` into a `String`, producing about 384 MiB peak RSS for a 64 MiB blob upload; testing this risk requires blobs of at least 256 MiB or the `ci/full` scale.
`Cas::Store` remains responsible for protocol and object identity, including ref resolution, manifest validation, blob-location translation, and committed-ref mutation.

The v2 Payload family keeps CABL constant-offset ranged reads and replaces header_hash with header_crc32c in the guard slot while leaving payload bytes unchanged Additionally, v2 changes CasEnvelope.header_hash to header_crc32c at [86,90), with [90,94) as a zero u32, while keeping the 94-byte core
v3 drops cas_blob hash_algo, domain_id, header_hash, writer_version, logical_size, and logical_hash because they are redundant, unvalidated, replaced by ch and bld, or already absent from code

Blob identity uses an in-body incarnation tag and an exact backend token for deletion; generations are absent from object keys, so the `404 → LIST` degraded read path is unnecessary and Keeper is optional.
Immutable CAS content uses a binary hashed format and mutable hot-path objects use protobuf; JSON, pack objects, and the write-only build-heartbeat object were removed from the format design.

`fanOutBlobUploads` takes `ThreadPool &` explicitly so the same inputs can be run through a size-1 serial reference pool and a size-N fanned pool in one process; production passes `Cas::blobUploadPool()`.
The fan-out uses `ThreadName::UNKNOWN` rather than adding a CAS-specific enum value to shared `setThreadName.h`.

Serial-versus-fanned equivalence compares stable fields, logical payload, and backend metadata state rather than backend token values because concurrent fresh and resurrect uploads can mint tokens in nondeterministic order.
For CAS, `createHardLink`, mutable `moveFile`/`replaceFile`, and `moveDirectory` must be staged eagerly in transaction order; otherwise MergeTree can read the old state before commit.

A conditional PUT with a large body and `If-None-Match` or `If-Match` can be deterministically rejected with HTTP 412 before the body is accepted, so `Expect: 100-continue` should be used above a configured size threshold.

The content-addressed `writeFile` implementation, including append read-modify-write, autocommit-inline versus content-blob selection, and the deferred-finalize lifetime pin, is moved from `DiskObjectStorageTransaction` into `ContentAddressedDiskTransaction`.
`ContentAddressedDiskTransaction` dispatches every staging operation directly to the metadata transaction in program order, including `writeFile`, `createHardLink`, and the `moveDirectory` re-key.

The manifest-trust adoption trade-off (D4 relink trust model, ordinary ReplicatedMergeTree interserver trust) means a genuinely-absent adopted blob is no longer caught at promote time — it becomes an fsck `dangling` finding instead of a promote `ABORTED`; this is verified unreachable in production by source-pin plus durable-edge, backed by an independent EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE consult and a per-test reachability proof. This also incidentally fixed the S13 soak-run-3 liveness brick where `republishRef -> promote ABORTED (condemned)` had left a table readonly forever.

The GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256 signer was implemented as a sigv4 variant (renamed constants: `GOOG4` key prefix, `goog4_request` scope, `x-goog-date`/`x-goog-content-sha256` headers) plus a precondition-header mapping (`If-None-Match: *` -> `x-goog-if-generation-match: 0`; `If-Match: <etag>` -> `x-goog-if-generation-match: <generation>`) and token extraction from the `x-goog-generation` response header, letting the existing CAS S3 backend target GCS natively via a `http_client = gcs_hmac` opt-in and a `TokenType::Generation` token kind.
A dedup-cache hit does not skip the occupancy HEAD; it avoids the body PUT represented by `CasBlobBodyPutAvoided`.

The CA write path historically spilled an entire part to `disks/ca/cas_scratch` before S3 upload: a 24 GiB part used about 24 GiB scratch and a 100 GiB part used about 93 GiB, so a part larger than local scratch was unwritable despite bounded RSS. Additionally, A CA write path can spill an entire 100 GiB merge to approximately 93 GiB of local scratch, so very large parts require streaming hash support or documented S3-native staging.
A single INSERT into a 256-partition table can take about 10 seconds because each partition piece performs a separate CAS commit with manifest, ref, and blob round trips.

`CasJsonWriter` reduced representative `BM_EncodeRefLogTxn` latency from 753 ns to 333 ns by bulk-appending one record at a time, but the proposed <=3x memcpy-floor gate was not met because the validating encoder remained about 10.8x above the 30.7 ns raw-copy floor.
Bulk deletion is rejected for GC because `deleteExact` must preserve token-conditional safety and report `TokenMismatch` without deleting the object when the token is wrong.
The HEAD-before-GET pair remains a protocol step under the standing veto; the proposed cache removes whole redundant edges and therefore does not remove the HEAD from an edge that is still fetched.

S3 bulk `DeleteObjects` is rejected for `pending_deletes` because it provides no per-object precondition, while `deleteExact` is safety-critical and backends that ignore its condition are rejected by `Cas::Probe`.

Comparing hot-tier consolidation snapshots via bare `checksums.txt` equality was rejected because MergeTree checksums are `CityHash128`, a non-cryptographic hash that must not gate a decision to skip reading bytes; inode witnesses / borg-style filesystem-identity caches were also rejected as side state alien to the CA model, whose identity primitive is re-hashing.
Out-of-band uploads under a staging prefix must be adopted through verified hash-then-publish copy-forward rather than trusted in place.
The format-freeze work for `B176` must review envelope TLV fields and make the streamed `gc/snap` codec preserve streaming, compression, and ordering semantics.

In the meta-descriptor raw-body plan, the absent-meta AND absent-body retry mechanism in putBlob's step (Task 3 step 5) is left as an open implementation choice between a sentinel value and a re-throw-ABORTED-and-retry approach; whichever is picked, putBlob and observeAndAdmitByMeta must stay consistent.
